chapter: Dance tastes, big bands and the boat
title: Influence of Vincent Lopez, Whiteman and big bands on Dixieland in New Orleans
summary: DeDroit explains that his band finished arrangements in big-band style with Dixieland choruses, dates big bands to the mid-twenties, and mentions signing with Vincent Lopez's office.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Do you think that the orchestras are like, we're trying to talk mostly about what I was mostly concerned about was up until about 1930, if you can kind of keep that in mind. Yeah. Do you think that orchestras like Vincent Lopez, Paul Weichmann, Leo Reismann, and so forth, had much influence on what people wanted to hear here in New Orleans? I think so.
What kind of an influence do you think it had? A bigger sound? Was that being part of it?
It was the big band song.

Dixieland, understand I never did stop playing Dixieland, but didn't call it that. Because when we finished the arrangement, we finished it in big band style. But when we got down to one of the special choruses, you could meet the five men that get up and give them a-
Just like Whiteman did sometimes. Yes, he did, he did. Like Mississippi Mud. Yeah.
Well, we'd have a number that, it was up in tempo, could be played Dixieland, and then my Dixieland group would get up. And then we'd modulate right back into the last chorus and go out to see it.
When did you first hear the term big band, or when did you first start using that? Was that-
Well, I only started using it, when did I start using it? I started using it recently, you know. They were all big bands. They were all big bands.
What years would you say that they started with a real distinctive big band style? Would it be about like the late twenties, or somewhere in there?

I would say the middle twenties. Middle twenties? Yes, yes. Duke Ellington and such, you know, and Ray Miller. You see, as I told you, I signed up with Vincent Lopez's office. Not that I needed a job, because I was working. But it's good to have somebody looking out for your interest, you know.
